svg.title: What a derivative connects
svg.desc: A derivative ties together four descriptions of the same local behavior: a changing quantity, an average rate on a short interval, the limiting instantaneous rate, and the slope of a tangent line. Begin at the upper-left box. A function gives an amount. Comparing two nearby amounts produces an average rate. Letting the input interval shrink produces the derivative. The derivative is also the slope of the tangent line, so the diagram closes by returning to the original graph. The arrows do not describe four unrelated formulas; they describe four ways to talk about one local change. A derivative ties together four descriptions of the same local behavior: a changing quantity, an average rate on a short interval, the limiting instantaneous rate, and the slope of a tangent line. Begin at the upper-left box. A function gives an amount. Comparing two nearby amounts produces an average rate. Letting the input interval shrink produces the derivative. The derivative is also the slope of the tangent line, so the diagram closes by returning to the original graph. The arrows do not describe four unrelated formulas; they describe four ways to talk about one local change. The visual uses labeled positions, solid and dashed line styles, and written descriptions so what a derivative connects does not depend on color. Caption: A derivative ties together four descriptions of the same local behavior: a changing quantity, an average rate on a short interval, the limiting instantaneous rate, and the slope of a tangent line. Reading order: step-one: First labeled stage in the upper left.; flow-one: Solid arrow connects the first and second stages.; step-two: Second labeled stage in the center.; flow-two: Dashed arrow connects the second and third stages.; step-three: Third labeled stage in the lower right..
